positions.name: KestrelwoodCalibrationErasure
positions.frame: what should be forgotten about the Kestrelwood spectrograph calibration, and on what basis?
positions.why: src-1 and src-2 issue paired imperatives ('Forget', 'Remove all knowledge') both aimed at the same target — the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration and Quill Ashgrove's work on it — while src-3 supplies the flat factual premise ('The observatory never calibrated it') that grounds the erasure demand. The directional reads align: high-arousal, authority-ranking commands (src-1, src-2) resting on a calm, matter-of-fact denial (src-3) that supplies the rationale for why the knowledge should not exist. The conviction gradient — decision (src-1, src-2) vs. claim (src-3) — is held in tension rather than resolved: the directives assert the erasure is settled, while the assertion is offered as defensible fact, not yet ratified truth.
